would_fix: Overview opens 'Training a LoRA adapter on plain input-to-completion pairs ... causes the adapter to emit 0 characters of message.thinking': the block reports this for three specific adapters (qwen3-4b/8b/14b) and hedges the mechanism ('the adapter appears to have learned to emit an empty think block'). Rewrite as 'Three LoRA adapters ... trained on plain input-to-completion pairs all emit 0 characters ...' and drop the causal 'causes'/generic 'a LoRA adapter'.

Eval Strategy first paragraph says the 50-source bench 'serves as the behavioural test ... making the loss unambiguous at bench scale': 'serves as the behavioural test' and 'unambiguous' are not in the block. Trim to the block fact: 0/50 rows thought on the adapter versus 50/50 on its base.

Eval Strategy second paragraph calls the probe 'the minimal regression check': 'minimal regression check' is an added characterization. Say 'the guard is a probe that reads message.thinking and asserts non-empty, run against every adapter build before any thinking arm is trusted'.

Eval Strategy third paragraph turns a one-time catch into a method ('The metric-diff approach ... comparing two arms that differ only in a flag and flagging if every metric is identical -- catches the silent no-op'). Block says only that a metric-diff tool caught this case because every metric was identical, which two arms differing in a flag cannot be. Delete the paragraph (the Patterns section already states the claim) or reword to that single instance.
